reasoning: Use two internally proved lemmas: (1) gcd(a,b)=gcd(a,c)=1 implies gcd(a,bc)=1, from multiplied Bezout identities; induction gives gcd(m_i,M_i)=1. (2) if gcd(a,b)=1 and a|z,b|z then ab|z, from Bezout; induction gives product divisibility. Choose u_i with u_i M_i congruent to 1 mod m_i and set x=sum_i a_i u_i M_i. Uniqueness follows by applying product divisibility to x-y.

summary: Explicit selector construction proves existence; a non-circular Bézout induction proves uniqueness modulo M.
